Paper: Yu, Wang, Wu - Defect detection for large-curvature highly reflective surfaces (polarization imaging + improved YOLOv11)
Physics: Light-propagation analysis; glare suppression by polarization
Polarization ground truth?: Physical measurement only (no separate ground-truth polarimetry)
Application: Surface defects on curved reflective parts
Difference from proposed method: Requires polarization hardware at deployment; detection only; no virtual polarimetry, no corrosion-specific optics, no uncertainty. We use it as physical/methodological inspiration only.

Paper: Enhanced Defect Detection in Additive Manufacturing via Virtual Polarization Filtering and Deep Learning Optimization (IEVPF + YOLO V5-W)
Physics: 'virtual manipulation of light polarization' (internals NOT yet read)
Difference from proposed method: CLOSEST PRIOR ART for the phrase 'virtual polarization filtering'. Must read before any novelty claim about virtual polarizers; our differentiators would be Mueller/Stokes-consistent analyzer, conductor Fresnel + geometry, PSRF, ensemble uncertainty, distillation, corrosion application - only if the paper does not already do these.

Paper: Lin, Yuan, Chen - RGB-to-Polarization Estimation: A New Task and Benchmark Study
Hardware: None at inference; polarization camera to build dataset
Physics: Mostly data-driven (benchmark of image-to-image networks incl. Restormer/Uformer per snippets)
Difference from proposed method: Establishes RGB->polarization as a task. We cannot claim it as new. Our setting adds conductor-specific physics, latent optical state, PSRF, corrosion tasks, and uncertainty/ensemble, and evaluates downstream corrosion utility.

Paper: GenPolar - Stokes-Informed Diffusion for Robust Linear Polarization Estimation
Physics: Stokes-informed: predicts linear Stokes channels, derives DoLP/AoLP analytically
Difference from proposed method: Strong generative competitor for RGB->Stokes; heavy (diffusion) vs our edge target; no metal/corrosion optics, no analyzer-optimisation or PSRF. Should be a comparison baseline if code is available.

Paper: Ba et al. - Deep Shape from Polarization
Difference from proposed method: Needs real polarization input; shape not corrosion. Informs ambiguity handling (pi, azimuth).

Paper: Lei et al. - Shape from Polarization for Complex Scenes in the Wild
Difference from proposed method: Real polarization input; shows ambiguity grows with complex materials/non-orthographic projection - motivates our uncertainty/ensemble framing.

Paper: Zhao, Monno, Okutomi - Polarimetric Multi-View Inverse Rendering
Difference from proposed method: Needs real polarization and multi-view; dielectric focus.

Paper: Nayar, Fang, Boult - Separation of Reflection Components Using Color and Polarization
Difference from proposed method: Classical separation needing polarization measurements; assumes illuminant-coloured specular (invalid for metals).

Paper: Kajiyama et al. - Separating partially-polarized diffuse and specular components under unpolarized sources
Difference from proposed method: Supports our rule 'do not assume diffuse unpolarized / specular fully polarized'; needs hardware.

Paper: Baek et al. - Image-based acquisition and modeling of polarimetric reflectance (pBRDF dataset)
Difference from proposed method: Reference measured polarimetric reflectance of metals; potential source of validation for our Fresnel/microfacet Mueller model; not an inspection method.
Recovers refractive index with hardware; shows what is identifiable only with polarization measurements.
Needs real polarization; scene-level neural fields (not edge).

Paper: Li et al. - NeISF (and NeISF++ for conductors/dielectrics)
Difference from proposed method: Treats conductors (NeISF++) - important physics overlap; hardware + multi-view + offline.

Paper: Kalra et al. - Deep Polarization Cues for Transparent Object Segmentation
Difference from proposed method: Shows polarization features improve segmentation (hardware); different material/task.

Paper: Corrosion segmentation (RustSEG; MCD-Net; J. Electron. Imaging 2019; pitting in gas pipelines)
Difference from proposed method: No optical modelling of glare or metal reflection; not copper/bronze cartridges (except heritage-asset microscopy study).

Paper: Metal heritage corrosion compounds on microscopic images (iron & copper)
Difference from proposed method: Closest copper-corrosion segmentation precedent; microscopy not field RGB; no polarization.
